title: Macaroni Cheese
subtitle: Creamy baked macaroni in a three-cheese sauce
excerpt: Macaroni in a rich bechamel with mature Cheddar, Gruyere, and Parmesan, topped with breadcrumbs and baked until golden and bubbling. The definitive comfort food.

recipe.sourceNotes: Macaroni cheese has been a British comfort food since the 19th century. The classic British version uses a bechamel (butter, flour, milk) enriched with Cheddar and baked in the oven with a breadcrumb topping. Thomas Jefferson popularized it in America after encountering it in France. The three-cheese approach adds complexity: Cheddar for sharpness, Gruyere for melt, and Parmesan for depth. Cook the pasta 2 minutes less than the packet instructions as it continues to cook in the oven.

recipeTools.notes: For the pasta and the sauce.

content.text: Make the bechamel properly: cook the flour and butter for a full minute to remove the raw flour taste before adding the milk. Add the milk gradually and whisk constantly to avoid lumps. Do not over-bake: the sauce should be bubbling and the top golden, but the inside should still be creamy, not dry.
Cook the macaroni in heavily salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions. Drain. Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6.

Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring. Gradually whisk in the milk, a little at a time, until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the Cheddar, Gruyere, half the Parmesan, the mustard, and nutmeg. Season. Add the drained pasta. Mix well. Pour into a large oven-proof dish.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the remaining Parmesan. Scatter over the top. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the top is golden and the sauce is bubbling at the edges.
